claim.why_it_matters: The subclause heading is transcribed as a plain paragraph, so a heading-based slicer finds no Syntax Rules subclause for INSPECT; its syntax rules (1)-(9) fall under 6.18.2 General Format.
claim.note: Its siblings are '### 6.18.4 General Rules' (page 328) and '### 6.18.5 Examples' (page 332); it should be '### 6.18.3 Syntax Rules'.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 327 (folio VI-95) shows '6.18.3 Syntax Rules' as a numbered subclause heading below the Format 4 box, styled like the other subclause headings. In page-327.md, line 17 is the bare text '6.18.3 Syntax Rules' with no '#' marker. A grep of specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md for heading lines matching 6.18 finds '### 6.18 THE INSPECT STATEMENT', '#### 6.18.1 Function', '#### 6.18.2 General Format', '### 6.18.4 General Rules' and '### 6.18.5 Examples', but no 6.18.3 heading. So the heading is missing, and syntax rules (1)-(9) are read as part of 6.18.2. One small inaccuracy: the siblings are not all at one level. 6.18.1 and 6.18.2 are '####', while 6.18.4 and 6.18.5 are '###'. The note's fix to '###' matches 6.18.4/6.18.5, but the sibling levels are themselves inconsistent.
verdict.corrected_description: The '6.18.3 Syntax Rules' subclause heading on page 327 is transcribed as plain text with no heading marker. In the markdown, INSPECT's 6.18.1 and 6.18.2 are '####' headings and 6.18.4 and 6.18.5 are '###' headings, so the level the restored heading should use depends on how that inconsistency is resolved.
